_comment: DISCRIMINATION CONTROL for layout/erc/adc_block.supply-spec.json's
`ties[]` declaration. Not an item-11 artifact -- never cite this run as
evidence about this block's well ties.
Byte-identical to the supply spec except for ONE character in the tie's
`tap_requires`: Pplus 31/0 instead of Nplus 32/0.
WHAT IT IS FOR. The committed supply run reports ZERO
`erc.missing_tie`, and a zero is only evidence if the check could have
produced a non-zero on this same stream. This control produces one.
Both implants really are drawn in ADC_BLOCK since issue #356, and they
are drawn in DIFFERENT PLACES on purpose: `Nplus` 32/0 marks the 25 n+
well taps, one inside each `Nwell` island, and `Pplus` 31/0 marks the
two p+ substrate-tie guard rings, both of which sit OUTSIDE every well.
So `COMP n Pplus` is a large, non-empty region that simply never lands
inside a well -- which is exactly the physical statement `p+ is not a
well tap` -- and every one of the 25 wells reports untapped.
EXPECTED OUTCOME: 25 `erc.missing_tie` findings and `erc_status:
"violations"`, from a NON-EMPTY tap region.
That last clause is what distinguishes this control from the
`tie-narrowed` known-gap reproduction it replaces (issue #340,
DR-0032). That one declared the same narrowing this repo's supply spec
now uses, and got the same 25 findings -- but from an EMPTY tap region,
because the stream drew no implants at all. Its findings were
*unfounded*: it would have emitted them whatever the layout drew, so it
discriminated nothing. This one moves the implant, not the layout, and
goes red for a reason that depends on where the tap actually is. Flip
the supply spec's own narrowing to 31/0 by mistake and this control and
the artifact would swap verdicts, which is the property a control is
supposed to have.
`run_erc.py` re-runs it and asserts the outcome above.
